notes_on_standings: Standings derived from weekly matchup winners through Week 11 (66 total wins across 11 weeks).
Tiebreakers used where applicable: head-to-head (when explicitly evidenced), then Points For as reported in weekly summaries.

league_trends_high_level.scoring_environment: Most weekly team totals cluster in the 90-120 point range; several outlier weeks pushed team totals into the 130-170 range (multiple weeks).
variance_drivers: Frequent high-variance QB outings (Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Justin Herbert, Joe Flacco in the week he appeared) produced large swings.
Kickers and D/STs produced several decisive outlier weeks (example: Steelers D/ST 22.0; Seahawks D/ST 21.0; kickers with multi-FG days and some zeros).
Bench management produced consistent weekly impact: across many weeks teams left 15+ and even 20+ point performances unused on benches, altering outcomes.

close_games.frequency: Multiple occasions per season so far.
representative_examples: Week 3: Here Comes McBride 108.12 – World of Hurts 108.02 (0.10 pts).
Week 6: Baker's Brownie Stand 89.68 – D.J. Chark Week 90.34 (~0.66 pts).
Week 11: Baker's Brownie Stand 101.82 – OHHHHHHH YEAHHHHH!!!! 99.98 (~1.84 pts).
Week 11: Gronk for my johnson 95.0 – D.J. Chark Week 93.54 (~1.46 pts).

notable_upsets_and_surprises: Several lower-projected teams won because opponents left major bench scorers unused or suffered starter busts (recurring across weeks).
TE and lower-roster skill players produced occasional massive spikes (Brock Bowers 37.3, Dalton Kincaid multiple high weeks, Jake Ferguson multiple TE TD weeks), changing matchup expectations.

recurring_decisions_affecting_outcomes: Leaving high-scoring QBs on the bench (examples across weeks: Justin Herbert, Matthew Stafford, Joe Flacco, Jared Goff at different times) — repeatedly noted as costly.
Bench players who produced 15-30+ points in multiple weeks (Romeo Doubs, Woody Marks, Jaxson Dart, Kayshon Boutte, Rico Dowdle) — many owners failed to insert them.
Aggressive use of defenses/kickers in weekly lineups — certain kickers/D/STs had high variance and swung matchups when started (Cameron Dicker, Jason Myers, Steelers D/ST, Rams D/ST).
Active use of waiver market: frequent FA adds noted across weeks (examples: Graham Gano, Raiders D/ST, Cam Little, Brandon McManus), indicating managers responding to short-term matchups.

examples: Leaving Justin Fields (27.14) or Jared Goff (33.96 / 24.8) on the bench in weeks where they massively outscored starters — repeated instances.
Bench QBs or WRs with big upside left unused in single-digit margin games (e.g., Keon Coleman, Keenan Allen, Mark Andrews on benches).
Targeting hot D/STs and kickers in specific weeks—several managers started defenses/kickers that then returned notable positive deltas (e.g., Seahawks D/ST 21.0, Steelers D/ST 22.0).
Waiver acquisitions that paid off: managers who added and started cheap breakout RBs/WRs (e.g., Rico Dowdle, Kimani Vidal) gained decisive edges.

season_trends.owner_behaviors: Made good use of bench/in-season adds (Browns D/ST and other bench TDs popped up); some inactives/BYEs were managed well (Purdy/other inactives noted).

player_level_notes: Bo Nix: one or more breakout weeks with high rushing/TD output (big impact when started).
Trey McBride: repeated TE scoring weeks, often exceeding projection and changing matchup outcomes.
team_summaries.playoff_relevance: Currently top seed; hot recent form and depth make this team a frontrunner for playoff success.

editorial_points_to_highlight: Week-to-week bench management has been the single most consistent narrative — include vivid examples each week (bench QBs/WRs who produced 20+).
Call out the sustained win streak of Here Comes McBride (6 straight) and the high Points For teams (Gronk, No Punt Intended, Baker) that yet sit outside the top seed.
Emphasize the growing importance of streaming defenses and kickers: the D/ST/kicker variance has decided multiple matchups.
Spotlight emergent positional narratives: RB breakouts and TE blowups have been league-defining this season.
data_limitations_and_caveats: Standings and Points For are taken from the most recent week-level summaries in the provided inputs and used for tie-breaking where explicit head-to-head results were available.
All statements are constrained to the performance and transactions recorded in the provided weekly summaries.
